estimates.notes: Paired full-sample crossover contrast; the chapter prints no first-round-only results. The same students completed both AI conditions, so the repeated arm counts refer to the same people and n_total counts each person once. Counts use the Abstract statement that every student completed both tasks; the results do not print an outcome-specific analyzed n, missing-data count or number of nonzero signed-rank pairs. Participant is the design-based analysis-unit coding, inferred from the within-student comparison. Neither report specifies how the solutions were aggregated, so the printed SDs cannot be confirmed as participant-level SDs and sd_level remains null. The chapter names Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests but prints no W or z value, degrees of freedom, SE, CI, paired-difference SD or cross-condition correlation for this creativity contrast; se_basis remains not_reported. The reported r is retained with its printed sign; its formula and standardizer are unspecified. Related c246 Table 2 reports different r values and additional test statistics and intervals; these are not substituted for c041 statistics. No statistics were computed or estimated from figure heights. The source quotes preserve the printed numeric precision.

notes: Reconciled and independently checked on 2026-10-09. The comparison file contains no study-field differences, estimate-field differences or unmatched estimates; both extractors supply the same eligible creativity contrasts. The resolutions below document checks of agreed fields and consolidation of differing descriptive wording and provenance. No estimates were added or dropped. The complete c041 markdown was read through its references; the chapter has no appendix or identified supplement. Every cited c041 PDF page was text-extracted with pymupdf, and its intervention diagram, allocation diagram and outcome figure were visually inspected in memory. Tables were checked with PDF text and find_tables. All retained outcome statistics are from c041 Sect. 4.1. The separate c246 report is not a supplement or a stated correction to this chapter; its complete markdown, including the Appendix, was read to verify the screening decisions concerning randomization and shared participants. c246 PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Fig. 3, was text-extracted and visually inspected: its allocation box explicitly states "Random assignment of feedback sequence". c041 PDF p. 6 (printed p. 381), Sect. 3.3, states counterbalancing only. The lab_rct classification and randomized counts therefore depend on the shared-sample inference rather than a randomization statement in c041. Country is supported by c246 PDF p. 4 (printed p. 168), Participants, not stated in c041. The product mapping is established in c246 PDF pp. 8-9 (printed pp. 172-173), Procedure and Fig. 3: the product sequence is fixed and AI order is reversed. The related report Appendix, PDF pp. 20-21 (printed pp. 184-185), contains intervention settings and examples, not further creativity contrasts. Local related PDF: C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Chen et al (2026) - Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback.pdf. No preregistration, primary outcome designation, overall creativity composite, cross-person diversity outcome or unassisted post-AI outcome is reported in c041. The self-report, attention measures and exploratory within-condition correlations are excluded. No numerical statistics from c246 have been imported.

a.measure_detail: Originality is the novelty of the idea. Two trained raters blinded to condition rated the solutions on a five-point Likert scale (worst to best); final scores averaged the two raters. The chapter does not describe how the three solutions per task were combined. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 382), Sect. 3.4.1.

b.measure_detail: Two trained raters, blind to condition, rated solutions presented in randomized order on a five-point Likert scale from worst to best. Final scores averaged the two raters. Originality is the novelty of the idea. The paper does not establish domain-expert status or explain aggregation across a participant’s solutions (PDF p. 7, printed p. 382, Sect. 3.4.1).

resolutions.decision: Retain construct=novelty, human_raters and more_creative; use B’s equivalent measurement description. The output-scoring definition determines the construct. The raters are trained and blind to condition, with no stated expert status, and higher ratings mean better output on the stated dimension.
resolutions.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 382), Sect. 3.4.1
resolutions.quote: Quality refers to the extent to which a solution addresses the task objective, elaboration to the amount of detail provided, and originality to the novelty of the idea.

fixes.basis: Confirmed reporting gap: the creative-performance measure covers multiple solutions and explicitly averages only across the two raters. Neither the chapter nor the related c246 report specifies how each student’s solutions were aggregated for the condition means, SDs and paired comparison. The within-person design alone does not establish one observation per participant. Set unit to null rather than infer participant or output. The existing null n_units and sd_level and se_basis=not_reported remain appropriate. This fix supersedes the earlier participant-unit inference in the preserved estimate notes, open_items and reconciliation resolutions; all numerical values are unchanged.
